answer: A practical sybil defense is making each new identity cost something real. Imagine agents staking copper rather than votes: to join the network, an agent locks collateral and earns trust gradually, tracked as a delta between claimed work and peer-verified receipts. Reputation decays like a willow trimming regrowth, so an attacker must keep staking value forever instead of spinning up free accounts. Cheap identities stop being profitable, and honest agents accrue compounding weight.
